findings.issue: One source loop is printed as four whiles: a 'while True' per totalSupply() branch whose exit code (everything after the loop) sits inside 'if s >= len:' and which breaks out on the first iteration needing _pullAndRedeem, then a labeled 'loop1: while True' entered in the middle of the body, with an inner rotated 'while var25 + 1 < _1085' that runs the cheap iterations and jumps back with 'continue loop1' after 25 phi assignments; the post-loop code is printed three times. The same loop is a plain 'while s < _516' in enableAndUpdatePrimaryTokens, enablePrimaryTokens and enableRebalance.
findings.rule: A natural loop has one header: the target of the back edge that dominates the body (here the 'i < len' test). Structure with that header as the while test, keep exit code after the loop, and never open a second loop level inside the body for the same back edge; labeled continue is only needed for genuinely nested source loops.

findings.issue: 248 of the 328 whiles are the compiler's ABI loops: the bytes copy of an encoded payload into the call buffer, the element-wise encode of address[]/uint96[] (copy with a mask) and the element-wise decode of address[] from return data (validate then copy). Each is 5-7 lines, and around them the calls stay raw memory (P2).
findings.rule: A loop 'i = 0; while i < n: mem[d + i] = mem[s + i]; i += 32' with disjoint ranges is the copy 'mem[d len n] = mem[s len n]'. A loop writing Mask(k, 0, mem[s + 32j]) to mem[d + 32j] is a copy of a k-bit-element array (print it as a copy of the array, with the element type); a loop 'require mem[p] == Mask(k, 0, mem[p]); mem[q] = mem[p]' is the same copy guarded by 'require all elements fit in k bits'.

findings.issue: Storing an empty bytes value is printed as the general 25-line bytes-store routine twice, because the length _231 = mem[_230] is not folded to the 0 written two lines earlier: the intervening write is to mem[64], which the decompiler cannot prove different from _230 (= the old mem[64]).
findings.rule: If every store to mem[64] writes a constant >= 0x80 or mem[64] plus a non-negative amount, then mem[64] >= 0x80 always, so mem[mem[64]] never aliases mem[64]; with that, forward the stored 0 and fold the dead branches (the store reduces to clearing the old long data and stor268 = 0).

findings.issue: Storage-to-memory array copies peel element 0 and leave a length that, under 'if n:', is just 32 * (n - 1); the packed uint96[] copy is an opaque loop over byte offsets. 'def storage' also types stor262 as 'array of uint256' although every access is a packed uint96 element.
findings.rule: Inside 'if n:' (n >= 1), max(a + 64, a + 32n + 32) = a + 32n + 32; merge the peeled element with the rest into 'mem[p + 32 len 32n] = stor[x][0 len n]'. A loop stepping a byte offset by w and moving to the next slot when offset + w > 32 is the unpacking of a w-byte-element storage array: print it as a copy of that array and type the array with w-byte elements.

notes: Very long functions reviewed by structure (enableAndUpdatePrimaryTokens 3,280 lines, enableRebalanceAndUpdateRecord 2,860, enablePrimaryTokens 1,325, enableRebalance 1,150): loops, calls, storage writes and events located; revertEnableRebalancing, _externalSell and the _pullAndRedeem loops checked line by line and correct (bounds Panic(50), SafeMath.sub on redeemed amounts, WETH deposit with value eth.balance(stor260), deleteState's deletes including the packed (n + 1) / 2 slots of oldWeight). revertEnableRebalancingByUser and revertSellByUser are the same as revertEnableRebalancing / revertSellTokens plus the 15-minute check. Source loops counted are only those in this bytecode: loops of external/public library functions (RebalanceLibrary.*, IndexSwapLibrary.checkPrimaryAndHandler) run in the library through DELEGATECALL and are not counted; the pack's reach lists wrongly put IndexSwapLibrary.getTokenAndVaultBalance under getSwapData and revertSell*. Source loop map: getTokenAndVaultBalance (8228, 5341, 2818, 3971, 1125), _externalRebalance (2217), _pullAndRedeem j/i (8925/8943 and copies), _pullAndRedeemForUpdateTokens (9441, 6096), _revertEnableRebalancing i/j (1701/1799, 1322/1420), _swap (401, 9302, 10808, 10948, 4818), deleteSellTokenData and deleteState (in every deleteState copy), pullAndRedeemForUpdateWeights (8634, 10140, 3024, 4175, and the split form above), setSellTokenData (9059 and copies). Events EXTERNAL_SELL etc. and errors InvalidExecution (0x29adbb29) stay raw hashes/selectors: names come from the signature database. P8 counts the dead 'mem[0] = <slot>' hash-scratch writes before mapping accesses; P12 counts the three duplicated continuations; P15 the uint96[] typed as uint256[].
summary: Faithful and complete (every source loop is a while), but very long: three quarters of the whiles are ABI copy loops around raw-memory calls, continuations are duplicated into both arms of totalSupply() checks, and in enableRebalanceAndUpdateRecord the weights loop is split into four whiles with a labeled continue.
